unsupported_claims: Graph embedding methods use MDS to handle millions of nodes by avoiding the O(n²) cost (accepts the false premise that MDS is used for efficient large-scale embedding).

Landmark-based MDS, sparse/approximate distance matrices, and Nystrom-style approximations make the cost scale roughly linearly (not in the passage; presented as how MDS-based methods handle millions of nodes).
rationale: The answer never corrects the false premise that the passage uses MDS to embed millions of nodes; the passage cites MDS only as a classical method with at-least-quadratic complexity that is too expensive at that scale. It instead supplies generic landmark-MDS details not found in the evidence, though it does mention the O(n²) cost of full MDS and admits it cannot see the passage.
